name: Evidence Sufficiency
description: determine whether the evidence set is sufficient to support any decision at all

name: Source Diversity
description: identify overreliance on one source class/community/account

name: Evidence Freshness
description: identify strategically important stale evidence

name: Contradiction Map
description: surface direct and indirect contradictions across sources

name: Corroboration Map
description: identify independently corroborated claims

name: Evidence Blind Spots
description: identify missing evidence classes needed for confidence

name: Anecdote-vs-Behavior Gap
description: contrast stated complaints/opinions with observed behavior

name: First-Party Evidence Gap
description: identify claims based only on public/secondary evidence

name: Source Bias Hypothesis
description: infer how source selection may distort the apparent conclusion

name: Confidence Ceiling
description: state the highest defensible confidence possible from current evidence

name: Problem Cluster
description: cluster evidence into underlying problems rather than topics

name: Root Cause Candidate
description: derive plausible root causes for a repeated pain

name: Pain Intensity
description: infer severity and cost of the problem

name: Pain Frequency
description: infer how often the problem occurs

name: Pain Urgency
description: infer forcing functions and time sensitivity

name: Segment Split
description: identify customer segments experiencing meaningfully different versions of the problem

name: Persona Role Map
description: distinguish user, buyer, champion, blocker and administrator

name: High-Pain Segment
description: identify the segment with highest evidenced severity/frequency

name: Problem Context
description: identify contexts/triggers in which the problem becomes salient

name: Problem Consequence Chain
description: map pain → operational effect → business effect → emotional/social effect

name: JTBD Statement
description: derive job-to-be-done candidates from evidence

name: Current Workflow
description: reconstruct how users solve the job today

name: Workaround Map
description: classify manual, software, service, spreadsheet, social and non-consumption workarounds

name: Non-Consumption Reason
description: explain why users do nothing despite a stated pain

name: Switching Cost
description: identify procedural, data, social, contractual and cognitive switching costs

name: Behavior Change Burden
description: estimate how much new behavior adoption requires

name: Trigger-to-Action Chain
description: identify what event causes a user to seek a solution

name: Habit/Retention Driver
description: identify repeated triggers/rewards that could sustain use

name: Adoption Blocker
description: identify friction preventing trial or continued use

name: Abandonment Hypothesis
description: explain why users may stop using an existing/imagined solution

name: Core Value Proposition
description: derive the most evidence-supported promise

name: Avoided-Loss Proposition
description: frame value as cost/risk/delay avoided

name: Gain Proposition
description: frame value as measurable upside achieved

name: Emotional Value Proposition
description: identify confidence/status/stress/reassurance value

name: Persona-Specific Proposition
description: adapt proposition by user/buyer/champion role

name: Positioning Statement
description: derive category, audience, alternative and differentiated value

name: Category Hypothesis
description: infer which category framing makes the product easiest to understand/buy

name: Differentiation Hypothesis
description: identify differences customers appear to value, not just product differences

name: Headline Hypotheses
description: generate testable landing-page headline variants grounded in customer language

name: CTA Hypotheses
description: derive calls-to-action appropriate to evidence/readiness and customer intent

name: Feature Opportunity
description: derive features directly from evidenced problems

name: Feature Anti-Opportunity
description: identify requested features not justified by evidence

name: Minimum Valuable Experience
description: derive the smallest experience that could deliver the core outcome

name: Concierge Version
description: identify what can be manually delivered before software exists

name: Wizard-of-Oz Version
description: identify which automated-looking behavior can safely be fulfilled manually for testing

name: Fake-Door Concept
description: derive the smallest credible demand probe

name: Workflow Integration Point
description: identify where in the customer's current workflow the product should enter

name: Product Boundary
description: define what the product should explicitly not attempt to solve

name: Feature Dependency Graph
description: derive feature prerequisites and dependent outcomes

name: Solution Alternative Set
description: generate materially different solution approaches to the same problem

name: Willingness-to-Pay Hypothesis
description: infer testable WTP ranges and confidence

name: Pricing Metric Hypothesis
description: seat, usage, project, outcome, asset, account, device, etc

name: Packaging Hypothesis
description: identify coherent bundles/tier boundaries

name: Freemium Suitability
description: reason whether free usage creates conversion/distribution value or cost leakage

name: Trial Design Hypothesis
description: infer what a trial must expose to demonstrate value

name: Cost-to-Serve Risk
description: infer expensive workflows or human/service burden

name: Gross-Margin Hypothesis
description: estimate major margin drivers needing validation

name: CAC Ceiling Hypothesis
description: derive maximum tolerable acquisition cost from current economics

name: LTV Driver Hypothesis
description: identify behaviors and business variables most likely to drive lifetime value

name: Monetization Failure Mode
description: identify reasons real demand may fail to become revenue

name: Direct Competitor Map
description: synthesize direct competitors and key evidence

name: Indirect Competitor Map
description: synthesize adjacent products solving the same job differently

name: Substitute Map
description: spreadsheets, services, internal processes, community, doing nothing

name: Competitor Complaint Cluster
description: aggregate repeated negative review/problem themes

name: Competitor Strength Cluster
description: identify incumbent strengths users value and should not be ignored

name: Positioning Gap
description: infer underserved combinations of audience/problem/experience/price/trust

name: Incumbent Indifference
description: identify opportunities too small/awkward for incumbents to prioritize

name: Incumbent Response Risk
description: estimate how easily an incumbent could neutralize the differentiation

name: Market Saturation Hypothesis
description: infer whether competition indicates demand, commoditization or over-supply

name: Precedent Failure Lesson
description: extract lessons from similar products/startups that failed or shut down

name: Channel Fit
description: rank channels by evidence quality and reachability

name: Evidence-Per-Euro Channel
description: rank channels specifically by validation signal per cost, not scale

name: Community Fit
description: identify communities in which the problem naturally appears

name: Search Intent
description: infer search queries and intent stages indicating active demand

name: Content Angle
description: derive content topics likely to produce useful validation signals

name: Outreach Angle
description: derive conversation openers based on evidenced pains rather than sales copy

name: Referral Loop Hypothesis
description: identify whether use naturally exposes/invites others

name: Virality Constraint
description: identify what prevents organic sharing or collaboration loops

name: Distribution Edge
description: identify founder/company assets that reduce acquisition difficulty

name: Channel Failure Mode
description: identify why an apparently attractive channel may not produce qualified users

name: Trust Barrier
description: derive why customers may not trust the solution/provider

name: Proof Requirement
description: identify proof, certification, demo or social validation needed for adoption

name: Privacy Concern
description: synthesize data/privacy objections

name: Security Concern
description: synthesize security objections and required assurances

name: Regulatory Constraint
description: identify regulation/licensing/compliance hypotheses requiring validation

name: Platform Dependency Risk
description: detect dependency on APIs/platforms/providers that could invalidate the model

name: Technical Feasibility Risk
description: identify evidence gaps around whether the solution can actually work

name: Operational Feasibility Risk
description: identify human/process scaling constraints

name: Reputation Risk
description: identify trust/reputation failure paths from the proposed behavior

name: Abuse/Fraud Risk
description: derive foreseeable misuse/fraud incentives that affect product viability

name: Riskiest Assumption
description: select the highest-impact/highest-uncertainty load-bearing assumption

name: Cheapest Disconfirming Test
description: identify the cheapest test capable of proving the hypothesis wrong

name: Interview Test
description: derive Mom-Test-style questions that avoid pitching and leading

name: Fake-Door Test
description: derive audience, message, instrumentation and pass/fail threshold

name: Pricing Test
description: derive behavioral pricing experiment and threshold

name: Concierge Test
description: derive manual test, sample, duration and success/failure threshold

name: Instrumentation Gap
description: identify what product analytics/event tracking is needed to answer a hypothesis

name: Source Acquisition Plan
description: identify which evidence sources can most efficiently close the gap

name: Discriminating Experiment
description: design a test that differentiates between two competing hypotheses

name: Replication Test
description: design an independent repeat/segment/source test for an apparently strong result

name: Executive Focus Points
description: identify what a decision-maker report should emphasize

name: Evidence Narrative
description: turn evidence into a chronological/causal story without overstating certainty

name: Customer Voice Summary
description: summarize recurring language, preserving provenance

name: Key Quotes/Examples Selection
description: choose representative examples without cherry-picking

name: Decision Memo Focus
description: identify the facts that should determine build/test/pivot/kill decisions

name: Investor Narrative Focus
description: derive market/problem/proof/risk points relevant to an investor audience

name: Sales Narrative Focus
description: derive pain/proof/outcome points relevant to buyer conversations

name: Research Report Focus
description: identify strongest findings, caveats and next questions

name: Dashboard KPI Focus
description: derive which metrics should be monitored because they resolve current hypotheses

name: Unknowns Disclosure
description: produce the explicit “what we still do not know” section for any report

name: Build/Test/Pivot/Kill Recommendation
description: deterministic/structured decision backed by evidence state

name: Pivot Candidate
description: generate a one- or two-variable pivot preserving strong dimensions

name: Kill Criterion
description: define evidence that should terminate the idea/hypothesis

name: Scale Criterion
description: define evidence required before allocating more resources

name: Venture Mode Fit
description: infer solo/indie/B2B/venture-scale operating assumptions and mismatches

name: Resource Fit
description: map founder/team assets and constraints to the opportunity

name: Portfolio Priority
description: rank multiple hypotheses/ventures by evidence, upside, cost and uncertainty

name: Expected Learning Value
description: rank actions by expected decision information generated per unit cost/time

name: Strategic Dependency
description: identify hypotheses that gate many downstream decisions

name: Opportunity Cost
description: identify what pursuing this option prevents or delays elsewhere

name: Cross-Cluster Bridge
description: find non-obvious connections between evidence clusters (Nodepad Ghost-style)

name: Second-Order Hypothesis
description: derive what follows if a first-order hypothesis is true

name: Third-Order Business Consequence
description: derive downstream business implications of a supported second-order effect

name: Alternative Explanation
description: generate plausible explanations for the same observation

name: Hidden Common Cause
description: infer a latent cause that could explain multiple problems at once

name: Tension/Paradox
description: surface evidence pairs that appear true but pull strategy in opposite directions

name: Adjacent Opportunity
description: infer an adjacent product/service opportunity from existing pain/evidence

name: New Venture Candidate
description: identify when multiple evidence clusters imply a distinct venture rather than a feature

name: Weak-Signal Emergence
description: identify low-volume but fast-growing or strategically novel signals

name: World-Model Update
description: synthesize the most important change to the current “brain” caused by new evidence
